                                   PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                              SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349



APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                             §
DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                             §                 BEFORE THE
TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION                         §
TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF                            §             THE STATE OFFICE
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE                         §
BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL                       §                        OF
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE                       §
PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,                          §              ADMINISTRATIVE
CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,                          §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS,                          §                   HEARINGS
SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                          §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                   §



                  KEVIN KENNEDY’S REPLY POST-HEARING BRIEF



       Kevin Kennedy ("Mr. Kennedy”), pro se intervenor, timely files this Reply Brief to the

State Office of Administrative Hearings ("SOAH") Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs")

regarding Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s (“Oncor’s”) and LCRA Transmission

Services Corporation’s (“LCRA’s”)(collectively, “Applicants’”) application for a certificate of

convenience and necessity (“CCN”) for Bell County East to Bill Hill 765-kV transmission line.

       Mr. Kennedy respectfully requests the SOAH ALJs and the Commission to properly and

rightfully determine this application does not meet PURA requirements and therefore requests

the Commission REFUSE TO GRANT the certificate.




KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                Page 1 of 15
                                         I. INTRODUCTION

        As required by PURA, the Applicants failed to establish a specific need for additional

service regarding this project or that the project has any ability to meet any need.

        As required by PURA, the Applicants failed to conduct proper routing studies which

adequately considered other factors, such as community values, historical values, or

environmental integrity.

        As required by the Commission’s substantive rules, the Applicants failed to comply with

the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.

        As required by the Commission’s substantive rules, the Applicants failed to mail notice

of its application to the owners of land, as stated on the current county tax rolls, who would be

directly affected by the requested certificate.

        The evidence has shown the ALJs should recommend DENIAL of the certificate, and the

Commission should ultimately REFUSE TO GRANT the certificate, due to the aforementioned

failures.

                   II. THE BURDEN OF PROOF IS ON THE APPLICANTS

        The burden to prove the project’s ability to address the need is on the Applicants. The

landowners or other parties are not required to disprove the project’s ability to address the need.

        The burden to prove the project has a sufficient, available, and dedicated source of

reliable, dispatchable power to supply the power required to address the need is on the

Applicants. The landowners or other parties are not required to disprove the project’s source of

power required to address the need.




KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                  Page 2 of 15
        The burden to prove the routing analysis complied with the Commission’s policy of

prudent avoidance is on the Applicants. The landowners or other parties are not required to

disprove compliance with the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.

       The burden to prove the routing analysis addressed community values is on the

Applicants. The landowners or other parties are not required to disprove compliance with

community value requirements.

       The burden to prove they obtained and properly used the current county tax roll in March

2026 for mailing notification of the application is on the Applicants. The landowners or other

parties are not required to disprove compliance with the notification requirements.

       The Applicants have utterly and completely failed to prove any of the above in the

application or through the presentation of facts into the evidentiary record. On the other hand,

though not required, landowner intervenors have produced substantial facts and evidence that the

Applicants did not comply with the listed issues and have not met the requirements of PURA and

substantive rules.



                        III. ABSENCE OF FACTS REGARDING NEED

       The Applicants have attempted to bolster their argument by conflating the need for local

Permian transmission projects identified in ERCOT’s Permian Basin Reliability Plan (“PBRP”)

with the separate and distinct PBRP import path projects. No one has argued that the local

projects are not needed, as described in the PBRP: “ERCOT’s identification of local needs

explicitly fulfills the PUCT's directive to “address extending transmission service to areas where

mineral resources have been found” and to “provide available infrastructure to reduce




KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                 Page 3 of 15
 interconnection times in areas without access to transmission service”. 1 These local projects are

addressed under separate dockets and are not at issue here.

         The Applicants attempt to confuse the issue by making countless unsubstantiated

statements of “need” that are not present in or associated with their application. If these

arguments are necessary to establish the need for the project, the Applicants should have

included this information in the application. The Applicants are sophisticated in the preparation

of applications to amend their CCNs. Why would this particular application be so deficient with

regard to need? The answer is simple, the need for the project has not been established by any

party. We have been told the sky is falling and if you will give up $4-billion and thousands of

acres of private land, we will do something, but that’s about as detailed as they get.

         ERCOT’s PBRP is a planning study, not a detailed engineering report. In reality, it

appears to be not much more than a cross between Chicken Little and the Boy Who Cried Wolf.

It asserts that power is needed in the Permian Basin, but it never states the specific deficit in

supply. It never states how much more power is needed at any specific location. It never states

the need at Big Hill or Sand Lake, or any other substation or switch for that matter. It never

describes how much power flows through Import Path 2 to address the need it never states. It

never addresses the obvious question of what the source of the unknown power flow from Bell

County East to Big Hill is. Imagine any business trying to respond to such a nebulous description

of need; they could not. Imagine being the guy who has to pay the bill.

         The PBRP and the application never justify the capacity of a 765-kV line with a transfer

rate needed. Without knowing the transfer rate, it is impossible to know whether a 765-kV is




1
    Oncor & LCRA TSC – 3 (PBRP) at pp.37-38

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 4 of 15
 needed. Maybe a 138-kV is sufficient; maybe nothing is needed. Who knows what is needed:

not the Applicants, not the landowners, and certainly not the Commission.

          The rate payers and landowners must not be placed under the heavy yoke of Import Path

2 based on a flimsy planning document and a deficient application. The Applicants are required

to prove the need for the project and the project’s ability to address that need; they have done

neither. The Applicants have done a masterful job of twisting and contorting, outside of the

application, without answering the question of need; however, this is not the OJ Simpson trial

that they are not Johnnie Cochran. This is a process requiring facts and the Applicants have

failed to produce the necessary facts. 2

          The People and the Commission require these facts. The Applicants talk all around the

issue of need, but they never explain how much power is needed, because they do not know. No

one knows, or at least no one has ever stated the precise need.

          ERCOT worked on the PBRP for most of 2024. The Applicants worked on their

application for 15 months. The Applicants have had another three months after the application

was submitted to get their ducks in a row, but their ducks remain in disarray. Landowner

intervenors keep pressuring the Applicants to state the actual need and the project’s ability to

meet that need but they are non-responsive.

                 The Applicants will not tell you in their Reply Brief or their Statements of Fact

                  how much power is needed at Big Hill or Sand Lake, because they do not know.

                 The Applicants will not tell you in their Reply Brief or their Statements of Fact

                  how much power the project delivers to Big Hill or Sand Lake, because they do

                  not know.




2
    PURA, Tex. Util. Code §§ 11.001-66.016 & 16 TAC §§ 25.1-25.508

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 5 of 15
                  The Applicants will not tell you in their Reply Brief or their Statements of Fact

                  the source of reliable power at Bell County East, because they do not know.

                 The Applicants will not describe in their Reply Brief or their Statements of Fact

                  the actual need for the project or the project’s ability to address the unknown

                  need, because they do not know.

                 The Applicants will not describe in their Reply Brief or their Statements of Fact

                  why a 765-kV is the correct size for this project; why a 765-kV is needed relative

                  to some other sized line, because they do not know.

          In the Applicants’ reply brief, they argue “ordering the development and construction of

generation facilities is outside the Commission’s and ERCOT’s authority” and “generation

cannot meet the reliability needs of the Permian Basin transmission system”. 3 Again, the

Applicants conflate issues and misrepresent the intervenor arguments. ERCOT and the

Commission does not need to order construction of generation facilities to properly consider

planned future generation in its modeling and studies. ERCOT must and does consider future

generation facilities to balance the load demand and supply in every topology model. The

Commission is responsible for administration of the Texas Energy Fund, which serves to

advance the construction of dispatchable generation. The intervenors simply point out what

common sense requires, that ERCOT was remiss in not considering the planned gas generation

in the Permian. The Applicants’ argument is unreasonable and without merit.

          Additionally, the intervenors do not propose generation only. The intervenors recognize

the local Permian transmission projects are necessary to bring power to where minerals are

found. The intervenors rightfully question ERCOT’s failure to use all tools in the tool box, which




3
    59475-6394 at p.10

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 6 of 15
 include new generation in the Permian that would obviously offset any need for inefficient cross-

state importation. The PBRP’s limited scope does not pass the smell test and the Applicants’

attempts to misdirect or confuse are not persuasive.

         This application contains no factual, quantifiable need so the application must be denied.

This application must not be allowed to stand on unproven oratories, vague platitudes and fear

mongering, which is all that the Applicants and the application have presented. The application

does not meet the certification requirements of PURA and therefore it must be DENIED.



       IV. FAILURE TO ADDRESS COMMUNITY VALUES, HISTORIC VALUES, AND

                                       PRUDENT AVOIDANCE

A.     Historic Ranches

         All routes must pass through one of either Route Link G51, G6, or G44. Route Links

G51, G6, or G44 are all located in Burnet County. Historic ranches are an important community

value of Burnet County. Historic ranches are an important community value of Texas and

Texans.

         Route Link G51 bisects and irreparably harms the historic integrity of the significant

Dillingham Ranch, owned and operated by William and Missouri Ann Dillingham and

continuously by their descendants, since originally acquired the ranchland in 1885. 4

         Route Link G6 bisects and irreparably harms the historic integrity of the significant

Taylor-Rose Ranch, owned and operated by William Taylor and continuously by his

descendants, since he originally acquired the ranchland in 1883. The historical significance and




4
    59475-2855

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                 Page 7 of 15
 integrity of the Taylor-Rose Ranch is recognized by the Texas Historic Commission and is

registered as trinomial number 41BT562. 5

       Route Link G44 bisects and irreparably harms the historic integrity of the significant Ater

Ranch, owned and operated by A.J. Ater and continuously by his descendants, since they

acquired the first portions of the ranchland in 1875. 6

       Route Link G44 bisects and irreparably harms the historic integrity of the significant

Barton Ranch, owned and operated by Wilson and Mildah Barton and continuously by their

descendants, since they acquired the first portion of the ranchland in 1855. 7

       The Taylor, Dillingham, Ater, and Barton families were all prominent families in Burnet

County. All four of these important families’ histories and contributions are described in Burnet

County History, Volume I & II, by Darrell Debo of the Burnet County Historical Society, which

was copyrighted in 1979 by the Burnet County Commissioners Court. The Burnet County

Historical Commission is actively collecting information about families that settled Burnet

County from 1900-2000. The history of the families that helped build Burnet County is a

significant community value and has been for decades. The heritage and integrity of these family

properties is important not only to Burnet County but to the State of Texas.

       No route option exists that does not impact at least one of these historic Burnet County

ranches, which are all paramount to the community values and historic record of Burnet County

and Texas.




5
  59475-4449
6
  59475-4218
7
  59475-4185 & 59475-4272

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                               Page 8 of 15
 B.     Schools, Churches and Habitable Structures

          The citizens of Florence and Williamson County do not want their little school children

unnecessarily exposed to harmful electric and magnetic fields. The citizens of Florence and

Williamson County want their churches protected. These facilities are held in high regard from a

community value perspective. For anyone to claim otherwise, would be absurd. Route Link F34,

is within 520 feet of both Lawler Baptist Church and Florence Elementary School. Applicants

made no attempt to and provided no evidence of any effort to prudently avoid these community

properties. The Applicants’ constraint maps show no constraint that would trump the safety of

over 500 little kids. 8

          Route Link N4 deviates from a straight line and bizarrely targets a cluster of habitable

structures including HABs 643, 644, 645, and 646. 9 Fig. 3-1G indicates no environmental

constraint that would restrict the Applicants’ ability to prudently avoid these structures. Why

target these habitable structures? Are the Applicants attempting to increase the habitable

structure impacts on Route Link N4 to make N4 less desirable?

          Under the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance, a “property line” would not trump

exposing four habitable structures to harmful electric and magnetic fields. Even so, Tracts 469 –




8
    59475-66, Application, Fig. 3-1B
9
    59475-66, Application, Fig. 3-1G   N4

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 9 of 15
 472 all show Stanley Kothman, per the Applicants’ Att. 12 (mailing list), 10 so the tract line is not

necessarily true property line. The application provides no explanation, no facts or evidence of

any kind, that the Applicants’ proposed exposure of HABs 643, 644, 645, and 646 to harmful

electric and magnetic fields is prudent.

           Applicants made no attempt to and provided no evidence of any effort to prudently avoid

this cluster of four habitable structures, in direct violation of the Commission’s policy of prudent

avoidance. The Applicants actually increases the construction costs in targeting these HABs by

introducing four turning structures, which are more expensive, rather than continuing the

alignment on a straight line.

           The Applicants failed to prove they comply with the requirements of community values

or historic values, or the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance, either in the application or

through the presentation of facts into the evidentiary record. The application does not meet the

certification requirements of PURA, does not meet the Commission’s substantive rules, and

therefore it must be DENIED.

      V.     FAILURE TO PROPERLY NOTIFY LANDOWNERS OF THE APPLICATION

           The Applicants did not collect current county tax roll data and did not utilize current

mailing addresses and did not notify all current landowners when they mailed their required

notification of application packets on March 26, 2026.

           The irrefutable example is Thomas and Christine Thies of Bell County. The Thieses

bought their lot with a new home (application Tract 3276; post-application Tract 3276.6) on

December 31, 2025 from a home builder, Brandon Whatley Homes, LLC. Brandon Whatley

Homes LLC bought the vacant lot from a developer, WDB Investments, on April 16, 2025.



10
     Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1 at p. 2419

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 10 of 15
 BWH Holdings LLC – Series 2 investments subdivided a 50-acre tract into residential lots on

August 9, 2024. 11 The Applicants’ data does not even reflect the August 2024 subdivision but

rather the parent tract. The Applicants’ mailing address used for the March 26, 2026, notification

of application is the address they collected in Spring 2025, when they mailed the public meeting

notices. They apparently had no time or inclination to adhere to the code and collect the current

ownership data in March 2026, but rather chose to just use the old data, as clearly indicated by

Anna Thornton’s RFI 12 and the Applicants’ note on the Att. 12 mailing list. 13

        On March 26, 2026, the Applicants mailed the notice of application to WDB Investments,

even though they had sold the property almost one year prior. The Applicants mailed the notice

to WMD Investments because rather than obtain the current county tax rolls, as required by 16

TAC 22.52, the Applicants used the same old 2025 tax roll data they had obtained in the Spring

2025 for use in mailing notices for the June 2025 public meeting notices. The Applicants divulge

this failing in their RFI response to Anna Thornton. 14 If for some reason that is not enough

proof, the Applicants also admit they used their 2025 public meeting notice addresses for their

March 26, 2026 application notices; specifically in a notation at the bottom of the Applicants’

Att. 12 – PUC Mailing List_Bell County to Big Hill, 15 which states, “*Supplemental address

based on returned notice from public meeting and additional tax card research”. This note tells

us the Applicants used the addresses from the public meeting, did not obtain current tax roll

addresses in March 2026, but rather only updated the old addresses by supplementing the thirty-

two public meeting notices that were returned with “additional tax card research”. The




11
   JKK PANEL EX 11 and JKK PANEL EX 13
12
   JKK PANEL EX 10 at p.17 (highlighted text) and p.21
13
   Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1 at p. 2454
14
   JKK PANEL EX 10 at p.17 (highlighted text) and p.21
15

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                               Page 11 of 15
 Applicants “tax cards” are not the current county tax rolls required by 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(3),

which the County Central Appraisal Districts update continuously. 16

       Based on our research we believe there could easily be 50-100 landowners who were not

notified of the March 26, 2026, application, due to the Applicants’ apparent cavalier attitude

toward notification and their failure to comply with 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(3). The actual number is

not known. There must be repercussions.

       With respect to notice of the public meeting notice, required by 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(4), in

their reply briefs, both the PUC staff 17 and the Applicants 18 argue 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(4) simply

requires at least one public meeting. The intent of 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(4) is to inform and engage

the public. It requires a “Direct mail notice of the public meeting must be sent by first-class mail

to each of the persons listed on the current county tax rolls as an owner of land within 300 feet of

the centerline of a transmission project of 230kV or less, an owner of land within 500 feet of the

centerline of a transmission project greater than 230kV”. It is ridiculous to assert that simply

holding one public meeting is a “get out of jail free card” for 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(4). The

evidentiary record proves the Applicants did not obtain current county tax rolls. The evidentiary

record proves approximately one-third of all affected property owners were not notified of the

public meetings. The evidentiary record shows the Applicants did not comply with 16 TAC

22.52.(a).(4). The reply briefs of the PUC staff and the Applicants are without merit.

       The Applicants did not comply with the Commission’s substantive rules, and therefore

the application must be DENIED.




16
   JKK PANEL EX 10 at p.30
17
   59475-6388 at pp.5-6
18
   59475-6394 at pp.2-5

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                 Page 12 of 15
                                              VI. CONCLUSION

          Despite of the extremely limited time provided and despite the steady stream of obstacles

presented by the Applicants, Mr. Kennedy has made his best efforts to rise to the challenge and

respond to the ALJs call to duty to intervene and to “provide the decision-makers the

information needed to reach a just and reasonable decision.”. Mr. Kennedy, along with many

other landowner intervenors, has brought forth the information necessary for a reasonable person

to determine that the application is severely lacking in content, justification, quality, and

accuracy.

          The Applicants repeatedly failed to comply with PURA, 16 TAC 25.101, and 16 TAC

22.52. Neither ERCOT nor the Applicants have articulated or proven any need, specifically for

the 59475 or 59182 projects, or that the 59475 or 59182 projects could actually address any

specific need, had one been stated. The pertinent statutes and codes require much more than what

has been presented in the application. 19

          The Commission’s CCN application process must not simply be an exercise in rubber

stamp approval; the lack of facts must be acknowledged. At some point, an application can be

found by reasonable people to be so lacking, to have so many holes, so many failures, so many

inconsistencies that it is obviously not worthy of further consideration. The facts show this

application is far beyond that point.

          Even though the CCN process has been severely curtailed by a dramatically abbreviated

180-day procedural schedule, it has exposed sufficient flaws in the application to require denial.

If this application is not the poster child for denial, what application will be? If this evidentiary

record does not show this application to be lacking merit, when will any application ever be



19
     PURA, Tex. Util. Code §§ 11.001-66.016, 16 TAC §§ 25.1-25.508 and 16 TAC §§ 22.52

KENNEDY 59475 – Reply Post-Hearing Brief                                                   Page 13 of 15
 denied? If this application is not denied, why are we wasting everyone’s time and money to go

through this process?

       The State’s duty to properly and lawfully exercise State agency discretion regarding this

CCN application is under a growing spotlight of public and political scrutiny. These proceedings

have shown the affected landowners, the rate payers, and the citizens of Texas just what kind of

operation the Applicants run. Over the course of the next few months, we are going to learn what

kind of operation the State of Texas is running.

       Mr. Kennedy respectfully requests the SOAH ALJs and the Commission to properly and

rightfully determine that this application is wrought with errors and omissions, does not meet the

certification requirements of PURA, does not meet the Commission’s substantive rules, and

therefore it must be DENIED.

       Mr. Kennedy again pleads with the State of Texas: Do not hand the Applicants the heavy

hammer of eminent domain and allow them to use that hammer to pummel the fine citizens and

landowners of Central Texas, along with thousands of acres of private property in our beautiful

Texas Hill Country, based on an application that has been shown to be lacking in every regard.

       Stop Import Path 2. If the State, the Governor, and the Commission choose not to stand

with the People, for the People, other jurisdictions most assuredly will.
